invariant_owner_layer.why: Both Contracts profiles enter this loop before interpreting the result of each gate.

problem_type: Contracts gate changes its own checkout after dependencies were installed
symptom: Post-merge receipt run 45331233660 failed later checks with Cannot find module p-retry.
direct_cause: The settings guard ran the real SessionStart handoff against the checked-out main. The handoff fetched and fast-forwarded from af64c5688 to 0250ecc5e after the install.
class_root: The behavior probe borrowed the checkout as its hook workspace and the Contracts runner trusted child exit codes without checking that subsequent gates still had the same input.
affected_population: Main receipt jobs and any CI or local Contracts run that uses the same checkout between steps.
internal_only_reason: The trigger and handoff are internal. Git supplies the state. The policy governing which checkout can change is owned by Nomi.
invariants: Registered settings commands execute in disposable directories.
Main follow declines CI before invoking Git.
A change to HEAD or porcelain across any Contracts step blocks the run even when the step reports success or is advisory.

door_reduction.why_not: The settings shell runner covers both control conditions; the settings axis and its parent dispatch probe selection; SessionStart keeps the interactive fast-forward entry; the Contracts CLI keeps its separate gate runner entry. Isolation removes the live checkout argument, without removing any of these direct callers.

generality_proof: All registered settings commands receive disposable workspace and home/cache paths regardless of event name. Automated main follow exits at its single entry. Both Contracts splits route every exit verdict past the same Git-state comparison, independent of the specific command and advisory list.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Owns the settings confirmation fixture and confines real hook execution to it.
Owns all automated main-follow eligibility before Git can run.
Owns snapshot comparison and per-gate attribution before exit status or advisory handling.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The two scripts select gates through the same CLI and runGateSuite loop.
The registered command invokes main-checkout-follow and the CLI delegates to followMainCheckout.
The real command receives the disposable radar cache, including nightly results, and observes the ordinary cached branch.

recurrence.reason: Future main commits can land during receipt jobs, and other gates can produce a visible Git mutation despite a zero exit code.
same_class_scan: door-map with roots scripts,tests/system over checkHookBehavior, checkSettingsGuards, runSettingsCommand, followMainCheckout and runGateSuite
Repository search for ff-only, run-gates-contracts and check:hook-behavior, followed through the registered SessionStart commands and both Contracts profiles.

prevention.invariant: Git HEAD and porcelain must match the start-of-step state.
prevention.failure_mode: Report the first step that introduces each change as blocking, update the baseline for attribution, and return 1 after the suite.
prevention.strategy: Remove the live settings probe, decline main following before any Git command in CI, and compare each gate against the previous Git snapshot.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old live-root invocation is replaced inline. There is no separate entry point or compatibility path to retire.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The checkout action and p-retry surfaced the bug. Neither controls when local probes or gates may change Git state.

migration: No persistent data changes. Existing local SessionStart continues to own interactive fast-forward.
residual_risks: The Git comparison observes state at step boundaries and sees the tracked/untracked porcelain entries, so it cannot detect a change reverted within a step or bytes changed under an identical pre-existing porcelain entry.
The historical hosted receipt is replayed with a local bare remote and cached radar input.
